questions.question: State Newton's three laws of motion with one example each.
questions.solution:
**First law (law of inertia):** a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force. Example: a passenger lurches forward when a bus brakes suddenly.

**Second law:** the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force, F = ma. Example: it is easier to push an empty cart than a loaded one.

**Third law:** to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Example: a rocket pushes exhaust gas downward and moves upward.

questions.question: Show that the horizontal range of a projectile is the same for complementary angles of projection. Find the ratio of ranges for 30° and 60°.
questions.solution:
R = u² sin 2θ/g.

For θ and (90° − θ): sin 2(90° − θ) = sin(180° − 2θ) = sin 2θ, hence ranges are equal.

R(30°) ∝ sin 60° and R(60°) ∝ sin 120° = sin 60°. Ratio = **1 : 1**.

questions.question: A Carnot engine operates between 500 K and 300 K. Calculate its efficiency.
Define linear magnification. A concave mirror forms a real image three times the size of the object placed 30 cm in front of it. Find the focal length.
questions.solution:
Linear magnification m = hᵢ/h₀ = −v/u.

Real image with |m| = 3 ⇒ m = −3 ⇒ −v/u = −3 ⇒ v = 3u = 3 × 30 = 90 cm.

Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v = 1/30 + 1/90 = 4/90 ⇒ f = 90/4 = **22.5 cm**.
